solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wine left in Metro, bizarrely

indicators.note: bizarrely says the letters of the fodder are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bottle of wine abandoned on the underground train, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarrely' rearranges METRO together with L (left), the 'in' simply placing the L among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Cricket club's extremely hasty admitting cunning US campaigner

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so cunning goes within the other letters

parts.note: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, based at Lord's in London

indicators.note: extremely takes only the two outer letters of the word hasty

parts.note: art is craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A cricket club rushes to let in a crafty American activist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' needs the cunning placed between the club and the ends of 'hasty', not in the middle of either piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Senator Joseph McCarthy led the 1950s anti-Communist campaign; Eugene McCarthy campaigned for president against the Vietnam War.

clue.text: Rally in park about beginning of year

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a local park
over can mean about, as in arguing over something

indicators.note: beginning of takes the opening letter of the word year

explanation.surface: A demonstration gathers in a park around New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' suggests a protest gathering; it means getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to regain strength, and a rally is a revival, an improvement after a setback.

clue.text: Rule book?

definitions.meaning: to book something is to reserve or request it

explanation.definitionFit: Order means both regulation imposed by authority and a request for goods or services.

clue.text: Plant with label attached, it's found near main road

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered main road, its 1 read here as the letter I
a tab is a small label attached to something
the 's is dropped, leaving the word it

explanation.surface: A labelled plant sits by the side of a busy road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its figure 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Wait-a-bit is a name for various thorny shrubs whose hooks snag passers-by.

clue.text: Promotion shown by stickers either side of vehicle

indicators.note: either side of puts the two sticker pieces before and after the vehicle

parts.note: an ad can be a sticker carrying an advertisement
cement sticks things together, a binding agent
a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: Advertising stickers on both flanks of a van promote something.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'stickers' is fair because it supplies two things, an advertisement and a glue, one on each flank of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement is moving up in rank or career, a promotion.

clue.text: Soldiers, distressed, plunged in confusion

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

indicators.note: distressed means damaged or agitated, so the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Upset troops are thrown into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled up means caught in a muddle or mess, in confusion.

clue.text: No end of punch: drinking too much could make you this

definitions.text: No end of punch: drinking too much could make you this

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the short piece goes inside
no end means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a blow is a punch
OTT, over the top, means excessive or too much

explanation.surface: A warning that endless punch drinking will leave you legless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of punch' reads as unlimited punch, but it is BLO, a blow missing its last letter; 'drinking' puts OTT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk, the result of excessive boozing.

clue.text: Newfangled gadget with label on

indicators.note: newfangled means newly made in a novel way, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A modern gizmo comes with a label attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tagged has had a tag, a small identifying label, fixed to it.

clue.text: Spy agency recruits scoundrel, chirpy sort

indicators.note: an agency that recruits someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a dishonourable man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: An intelligence service signs up a rogue who turns out to be cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is an insect famous for its loud chirping song, so a playful description of one.

clue.text: Archdeacon's appearing during, say, late church service

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven, plus the S of the 's
a performer who is appearing is on stage, on

explanation.surface: A senior cleric turns up for a service held in the late afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, held towards the end of the day.

clue.text: Return translation after lessons in religion

indicators.note: after places the translation following the religion lessons

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to a translation after their religious studies lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversion is a going back to a former state, a return.

clue.text: Conscious in accommodation near Scottish location, overlooking loch

indicators.note: in a down answer overlooking means sitting above, so the island comes before the loch

parts.note: taken as written
a tent is camping accommodation
Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: Someone is aware, staying in lodgings near a Scottish spot with a view of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscious in the sense of deliberate matches intentional, done on purpose.

clue.text: Coffee and butter up endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means both end letters of the synonym are dropped

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them

explanation.surface: A café order: coffee, and someone sweet-talking without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: Wear this red, crumpled material

indicators.note: crumpled says the fodder letters are crushed into a new shape

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on a red, creased piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRIS TWEED is a hand-woven woollen cloth from the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris tweed is a famous woollen fabric, so an example of cloth.

clue.text: Island with noise and bustle? Several islands

indicators.note: bustle is busy commotion, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: An isle full of noise and busy activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation made up of thousands of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Cricketer getting single in match? Most peculiar

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer

indicators.note: in puts the single inside the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring one run in a Test match; how very odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty is slang for eccentric or crazy, so the superlative is most peculiar.

clue.text: Town close to Folkestone in road near channel

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the road abbreviation
close to means the last letter of the word Folkestone

parts.note: a ditch is a narrow channel for water

explanation.surface: Directions to somewhere near Folkestone, on a road by the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Redditch is a town in Worcestershire in the English Midlands; Folkestone is a Kent port on the Channel, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Redditch is an English town, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Girlfriend keeps private place for crockery item

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a date is a romantic partner one goes out with
inner thoughts are private ones
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A girlfriend has a secret spot where she stores dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner plate is a large flat dish, one of the pieces in a set of crockery.

clue.text: Homeless dogs beneath street lights

indicators.note: in a down answer beneath means the lights come below the street

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Abandoned dogs huddle under the street lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are animals with no owner wandering loose, such as ownerless dogs.

clue.text: Sausage provided by woman, Pierre's friend

parts.note: Sal is a woman's name, short for Sally
ami is French for friend, Pierre being a typical Frenchman

explanation.surface: A woman brings a sausage, supplied by her French pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced Italian sausage.

clue.text: Work out temperature drops?

parts.note: rain falls as drops of water

explanation.surface: A question whether exercising makes your body heat fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' looks like a verb about temperature falling; it is a noun, the drops of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to exercise, as athletes do when they work out.

clue.text: In time, I'll get married, it's suggested

parts.note: taken as written
the 'll is a link, leaving the letter I
to mate is to pair up, here used for getting married

explanation.surface: Someone hints that they will wed eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate something is to hint at it, to suggest it indirectly.

clue.text: Name of female murder victim married earlier

indicators.note: earlier places the married abbreviation before the victim

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim

explanation.surface: A news report naming a woman who was killed, wed earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Putting together a musical work in German

parts.note: a mass is a choral setting of the Eucharist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is assembling a German composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassing is gathering things up into a heap, collecting them together.

clue.text: Tar, black, put round about base

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

indicators.note: put round says the black piece encircles the abbreviation for about

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap black tar around the foot of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of low and contemptible matches abject, wretched and degraded.

clue.text: Fit odd numbers of unit in farm building

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the farm building

parts.note: a stable houses horses on a farm

indicators.note: odd numbers means the first and third letters of the word unit

explanation.surface: Odd items of a unit are fitted into a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit and suitable both mean appropriate for a purpose.

clue.text: Spot British group near church

parts.note: a lot is a set or group of things

explanation.surface: Someone sees a crowd of Britons beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is a blemish or mark, a spot on a surface.
